parts:
The no-go holds. I verified it three ways and then spent the bulk of the effort trying to break it; nothing gets through. Memo 12 with the full audit is saved to the project alongside the new lab and its results.

**The proof itself.** The identity-theorem argument is correct and I re-derived it with every constant shown. One premise even weakens: it's enough that the domain *meets* the hyperbolic locus at all, since any hyperbolic point perturbs to a strictly hyperbolic one with a real-open neighborhood inside H. The useful summary form is: an analytic subset of a connected open in Cᵈ either contains no open piece of Rᵈ or is everything — so no analytic set can separate the hyperbolic reals from the non-hyperbolic reals in *either* orientation.

**Against Pool.** All eight load-bearing citations in memo 11 are verbatim-correct in the memoir, including H² as the obstruction group (so memo 10's inversion really was an error), N* = O(−1,−1) for ambitwistor space, and Theorem V.2's "YM equations ⟺ third-order extension" — the exact shape the no-go targets. The "k ≥ 1" in Theorem IV.4(b) is a genuine typo in the printed memoir; memo 11's "read as k ≥ 2" is the right fix, and V.2's proof only uses k = 2.

**Computations.** The original lab reproduces to the digit. I then replaced the float SVD with a tolerance-free certificate: integer-root samples, exact ranks over two prime fields. The hyperbolic quartic locus supports no polynomial identity through degree 7 (one past the original), sextics through degree 5, and the discriminant control has exact nullity 1 at K = 6 with kernel equal to the discriminant coefficient-for-coefficient mod both primes.

**Ways around it — all closed, several by arguments stronger than memo 11 needed.** Infinitely many conditions die individually; "vanishes at *some* order" dies by Baire; all constructible conditions die (rank conditions, jumping loci, dimension jumps of the obstruction group, "class ≠ 0" orientations); all-orders/formal extension is analytic and dies; reparametrizations and subfamilies (root space, the de Bruijn–Newman line) die; sufficient-only criteria force a discrete zero set inside Rᵈ — impossible for the ambitwistor obstruction specifically, whose zero locus is the positive-dimensional YM family, and structurally useless in general; and the no-go extends beyond the holomorphic category to anything *real-analytic across the discriminant*, killing ρ-equivariant equational retreats too. The sharpest formulation, made exact by the lab's closed form Σσ² = max(0, −disc)/2: what's excluded isn't "equations" per se — that *is* an equation cutting out exactly H — but any condition analytic across the discriminant, which is all holomorphic geometry can produce. The only survivors are memo 11's own two redirects (inequalities; σ-type/CR data non-analytic at the discriminant), and both land back at the brief's Proposition 1 objection. PROGRAM_CLOSED stands.

Sources: project docs `claude/memo11_holomorphic_nogo.md`, `claude/lab_holomorphic_nogo.py`, `claude/lab_holomorphic_nogo_RESULTS.txt`, and the project file `MEMO_65_358.E.pdf`; new docs written: `claude/memo12_nogo_verification.md`, `claude/lab_nogo_verify.py`, `claude/lab_nogo_verify_RESULTS.txt`.
